checks.covers: An options object that sets rejectUnauthorized to false
checks.misses: Verification switched off through environment variables or other HTTP libraries; a custom check that is too lax

checks.covers: requests calls with verify=False and ssl._create_unverified_context
checks.misses: Other HTTP clients; verification switched off through environment variables or a session attribute

checks.covers: tls.Config with InsecureSkipVerify set to true, and assignments of that field
checks.misses: A custom VerifyPeerCertificate that accepts everything; other ways of building the configuration

checks.covers: Server certificate validation callbacks that always accept, and the accept-any-certificate validator
checks.misses: Callbacks that are not literally true; other clients and platform settings

checks.covers: reqwest, openssl and rustls settings that accept invalid certificates or host names or install a custom verifier
checks.misses: Other TLS crates and wrappers; types not imported by their short names

checks.covers: Trust managers whose server check is empty, host name verifiers that always accept, and trust-all strategies
checks.misses: Trust-all logic written in other shapes; other libraries

checks.covers: cURL options that turn off peer or host verification
checks.misses: Other HTTP clients and stream contexts

entries.why: A client that turns certificate verification off accepts any server certificate, which is the failure the requirement guards against; each rule flags the literal ways its language switches verification off.
